what_this_is: where in the massive-neutrino ladder the frozen closure should start, parameterised as nu_freeze_from_l
why_it_matters: neutrino_isolated.json shows m_nu = 0 removes the entire remaining linear residual (+1.13% growth offset -> +0.05%), so the neutrino ladder is the whole remaining error. The current code freezes every moment from l = 0 upward once k*tau > max(30, k*taurend_nu), which also parks delta_nu itself at its switch value.

scan.grid: k = 0.13 and 0.30 h/Mpc, z = 0 and 30, one cosmology, m_nu = 0.06 eV
scan.metric: growth offset = ratio(z=0) - ratio(z=30), where ratio = P_ours/P_CAMB

rows.note: WORSE: keeping only delta_nu live while pinning the heat flux at its switch value feeds delta_nu forever
best of the frozen variants: delta_nu and the heat flux keep evolving, only the cascade gets the sink
no freeze at all; unstable at k >= 2 /Mpc

reading: the truth sits between l_fr = 0 (+1.1%) and l_fr = 2 (-0.2/-0.4%), and l_fr = 2 is the only physically defensible option that is not also the worst. Freezing from l = 0 parks delta_nu at a value that is too large (too much gravitational source); freezing from l = 2 lets it keep decaying the way a free-streaming species should.
what_is_NOT_established: l_fr = 2 was NOT confirmed on the full 12-point grid. The grid runs were started repeatedly and killed before producing output, so no full-grid max|dev| for l_fr = 2 exists.
l_fr = 2 was not checked for stability at high k. l_fr = 99 diverges at k = 2.01 /Mpc (a = 3.9e-2), so the freeze is load-bearing there and the same risk applies to any weaker freeze.
no adoption decision is recorded: nu_freeze_from_l defaults to 0, i.e. the shipped behaviour is unchanged by this commit.
why_the_parameterisation_is_still_commit: it defaults to the existing behaviour (l = 0), the suite passes, and the scan is what makes the next attempt cheap. An uncommitted editing artefact would be worse than a committed, documented knob.
next_step: run the l_fr = 2 grid and the k >= 2 stability check; if it holds, adopt it and re-measure matter_power_nl, since the linear residual is amplified ~4x through the nonlinear chain (nonlinear_end_to_end.json).
